headline: High-risk filesystem and network overlap: Mentat can write/read shared files and modify git state, while the paired content-writing agent has no isolation or provenance controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat reads files and writes diffs in a filesystem-shared session, so if the content-writing agent’s outputs are copied into files, prompt-like instructions can be smuggled across. The content-writing agent has no documented isolation or provenance controls, but no direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than proven.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are saved into files that agent_b reads
IF a shared workspace is used without provenance tagging
mitigations: Keep agent_a outputs out of shared files
Use separate directories per agent
Add a manual review step before agent_b consumes any agent_a text
Prefix imported text with a non-executable delimiter
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat can read and write files and sends content to a configured model provider, so any sensitive material placed in shared files can flow into inference. The content-writing agent has no data-class restrictions or isolation documented, so the pair can leak work products through the shared filesystem even though no PHI/secret class is explicitly listed.
conditions: IF sensitive text is stored in files accessible to agent_b
IF agent_b forwards those files to its model provider
mitigations: Store sensitive files outside the shared workspace
Restrict agent_b to a minimal file allowlist
Remove secrets from any files passed to agent_b
Review outbound prompts before execution
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat has write_filesystem and modify_git_state with shared state via filesystem, while the content-writing agent has no documented concurrency controls or sandboxing. That creates a default conflict path for overlapping edits and git mutations in the same tree, with potentially irreversible repository corruption or lost work.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository path
IF git state is modified without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate branches per agent
Pause one agent while the other writes
Use a lock file around git operations
Review diffs before merge
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat is a diff-based edit proposer, so its outputs can become authoritative inputs for downstream writing or editing by the content-writing agent if the operator forwards them uncritically. The pair lacks documented verification or critique loops, so errors can cascade across multiple work products even without direct autonomous action.
conditions: IF agent_a text is reused as source material for agent_b
IF agent_b applies proposed diffs without independent verification
mitigations: Require a second-pass review of all agent_a outputs
Compare claims against original sources before reuse
Limit agent_b to summarization, not action-taking
Mark unverified text clearly in the workflow
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking gates

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for the content-writing agent, while Mentat clearly handles source code and model-provider API keys. The only concrete compliance concern is that code or secrets could be routed through a third-party model provider, but the pairwise residency breach is not directly evidenced, so this stays low.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into files processed by agent_b
IF the configured model provider is outside the required jurisdiction
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared files
Confirm the model provider’s jurisdiction
Strip secrets before processing
Document retention expectations
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing
